content:
caroline: Quick brain-dump — I put together a sketch for a small 'decomposed burn' dashboard prototype. Goal: show per-invocation token burn with the cache savings broken into explicit components (kv-prefix hits, prefix cache hits, and model-side short-circuit savings), plus a per-model/unit-econ column and a tiny what-if slider to simulate routing/quota changes.

mike: Nice. Two quick asks: (1) sampling control (we need to be able to toggle sample rate) and (2) per-model granularity (not just model family).

ben: Do we actually have the telemetry fields to support this level of decomposition? I remember we emit total_tokens and cached_tokens, but do we emit reason for cache hit (prefetch vs hotpath vs kv)?

caroline: We do have event tags for: invocations.tokens.total, invocations.tokens.cached, cache.hit_reason (prefetch|hotpath|kv), model.variant_id, route, tenant_id. The missing piece is join keys for session-amortized prefetch credits.

alice: Quick SQL for the UI backend to compute avg split over a window (pseudo-SQL):
```
SELECT
  route, model_variant,
  AVG(total_tokens) AS avg_total,
  AVG(cached_tokens) AS avg_cached,
  AVG(CASE WHEN cache_hit_reason='prefetch' THEN cached_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS avg_prefetch_saved
FROM invocation_tokens_daily
WHERE ts BETWEEN :start AND :end
GROUP BY route, model_variant;
```

ben: Thanks. The big ops question — can we do amortized prefetch crediting per-tenant cheaply? If we attempt right-join per-session we'll explode cost.

sarah: We should pre-aggregate in the billing pipeline: per-minute per-tenant aggregates with fields (total_tokens, cached_tokens_prefetch, cached_tokens_hotpath, model_variant). Join in dashboard by tenant+route at query time — small footprint.

mike: Prefetch vs hotpath is important for routing preview. When you move a route to a cheaper model variant we need to show both the raw token delta and the *effective* paid tokens (post-cache).

caroline: UI thoughts: show a compact sparkline + 3 columns: raw tokens, cache-saved tokens (expandable breakdown), and effective paid tokens. Add a "preview routing change" toggle that runs a simulation on the selected time window and shows incremental cost delta. Also show a 1k-token unit-econ cell for quick comparisons.

ben: Also add a confidence band (sampling variance) when sample rate < 100%. Use WLS smoothing for noisy tenants.

alice: UX nit: label the what-if slider clearly and include a tooltip: "Preview assumes the same request shape and cache hit rates unless otherwise selected." And put a small notice when sampling <50%: "estimates may vary". :warning:

launch-bot: Prototype deployed to staging: /dash/decomposed-burn v0.1 — collect feedback @eng-platform

mike: Checked staging — awesome start. Found one bug: Y axis scales by tenant peak and squashes others. Also the model_variant label overflows in mobile.

caroline: Good catch on scaling. For the axis, let's add an auto/percentile toggle (auto uses 95th percentile). For labels we can collapse variant to short form with hover expand.

ben: Back-end schema sketch for the pre-agg table (proposal):
```
table invocation_tokens_minute (
  ts_min bigint,
  tenant_id varchar,
  route varchar,
  model_variant varchar,
  total_tokens int,
  cached_tokens_prefetch int,
  cached_tokens_hotpath int,
  invocations int
)
```
We store minute-level sums and compute means over ranges. Keeps query cheap.

sarah: Q: what about quantized vs full-precision fallback? We need to account for variant_cost_per_token mapping so the dashboard can compute dollars. There should be a small lookup table model_variant_cost(model_variant, cost_per_token_microcents).

caroline: Agreed — route policy will pass variant id into telemetry, and the UI compute will read cost lookup. We'll include the mapping in the pre-agg join.

alice: Also add a "rollout preview" mode that ties into the rollout API: pick a canary % and the UI shows estimated spend under that split. Could be useful for sales demos.

ben: We need to be careful with sample bias when simulating routing percentages; document assumptions in the UI.

mike: Timeline idea: backend pre-agg + cost mapping in 1 week, UI prototype + canary preview toggles next week behind a feature flag. SRE: keep retention at 30 days for minutely pre-agg to control storage.

caroline: Sounds good. I'll create tickets: ENG-11234 (pre-agg pipeline), PLAT-11235 (dashboard backend), FEAT-11236 (UI + feature flag). I'll add acceptance criteria and link the schema above.

mike: ack. I'll triage the axis/mobile issues after ENG-11234 lands.

ben: thumbs up. Also adding a short checklist in the ticket: sampling docs, variance note, model-cost table, and rollout API hook.

caroline: Thanks team — will circulate the mock PNG and link once it's in the ticket. :sparkles:
